class swiftlet.lightcone_projections.BeamProjection(vector, angular_diameter, redshift_range, cosmology=None, slice_thickness=None, store_snapshot_filename=None)[source]

Bases: object

Class for making simple projects of past lightcone beams.

Define the beam and the slice through it to project.

Parameters:

  • vector (numpy.ndarray) – direction vector as an array of 3 floats

  • angular_diameter (float) – angular diameter in degrees

  • redshift_range (sequence of two floats [z_min, z_max]) – redshift range to read

  • cosmology (astropy cosmology object or str) – cosmology object of the simulation, or a path to a snapshot to read it from

  • slice_thickness (int, float or unyt.unyt_quantity (units of Mpc or equivalent)) – thickness of the slice [Mpc], length along the z-axis, of particles

property gas_particle_data

Gas particle data in the slice.

property dm_particle_data

DM particle data in the slice.

Rotate the particles and keep only those in the slice.

Parameters:

  • particle_properties (list) – properties of the particles to keep

  • slice_thickness (unyt.unyt_quantity (units of Mpc or equivalent)) – thickness of the slice [Mpc], length along the z-axis, of particles

  • ptype (str) – particle type, “Gas” or “DM”

add_property_to_slice(dset_name, dset, ptype)[source]

Add additional properties to the slice particle data.

Parameters:

  • dset_name (str) – name of the property

  • dset (unyt.unyt_array or np.ndarray) – values of the property for all particles read, before selecting the slice

  • ptype (str) – particle type, “Gas” or “DM”

place_particles_in_slice(gas_particle_data, gas_property_names, slice_thickness=None, dm_particle_data=None, dm_property_names=None, xy_buffer=10.0)[source]

Add particles in the slice to the lightcone.

Parameters:

  • gas_particle_data (lightcone_io.IndexedLightconeParticleType for 'Gas' or a str) – gas particle data or a path to the particle lightcone

  • gas_property_names (list) – properties of gas particles to add to the slice. If None then essential properties are assumed [“Coordinates”, “ExpansionFactors”,”SmoothingLengths”]

  • slice_thickness (int, float or unyt.unyt_quantity (units of Mpc or equivalent)) – thickness of the slice [Mpc], length along the z-axis, of particles

  • dm_particle_data (lightcone_io.IndexedLightconeParticleType for 'DM' or a str) – dark matter particle data or a path to the particle lightcone that contains dark matter particles.

  • dm_property_names (list) – properties of dm particles to add to the slice. If dm_particle_data != None and dm_property_names is None, all properties are loaded by default [“Coordinates”,”ExpansionFactors”]

  • xy_buffer (float or int) – distance [Mpc] between the min and max position of a particle and the boundary of the slice.

project_properties(project_particle_properties, snapshot_filename=None, resolution=1024, assign_units=None, ptype='Gas', periodic=False, parallel=False, weight=None)[source]

Project the selected properties for a given particle type.

Note that, the projections are surface denisties unless a weight given.

Returns a list of 2D histograms, one per property, for a given particle type.

Parameters:

  • project_particle_properties (list) – properties to project

  • snapshot_filename (str) – path to a snapshot, used for its metadata and cosmology

  • resolution (int) – number of pixels along each axis of the projection

  • assign_units (list) – units of each property. If None, use the units of the slice data

  • ptype (str) – particle type, “Gas” or “DM”

  • weight (str) – property to weight by, e.g. “Masses” for mass weighted projections. If None, project surface densities

  • periodic (boolean) – If True, treat the snapshot box as periodic when projecting. Periodic copies of the particles appear if the projected region is larger than the box

  • parallel (boolean) – If True, use parallel backend of swiftsimio with projections.

beam_plot()[source]

Plotter for this beam, using the current cosmology, angular diameter, redshift range and axes extent.

split_beam_plot(numb_wedges, projection_data, colour_maps, axs=None, filename=None, angular_diameter=None, cosmology=None, redshift_range=None, axes_extent=None, update_badcol=True, figsize=(7, 7), titles=None, norms=None, **kwargs)[source]

Create plot of the whole beam, split into separate wedges.

Returns list of each projected wedge.

Parameters:

  • numb_wedges (int) – number of wedges or different projections to show in the beam

  • projection_data (list) – nested list containing different segments of the beam the 2D array to plot and a tuple with the min and max values shown in the img [2D array, (min, max)]

  • colour_maps (list) – list of colour maps for each segment of the beam

  • axs (matplotlib.axes._axes.Axes) – Default=None, If None create a new axes for the plot, otherwise use the axes given

  • filename (str) – None, if given, write plot to this file

  • angular_diameter (float) – total angular diameter of beam in degrees

  • cosmology (astropy cosmology object, astropy.cosmology.flrw.w0wacdm.w0waCDM) – the simulation’s cosmology model

  • redshift_range (list, np.ndarray or tuple) – maximum and minimum redshift of the beam shown

  • axes_extent (list) – Extent of the plot’s axes, in coordinate space. If None, then use the extent defined by the coordinates of the particles added to the slice.

  • update_badcol (boolean) – If true, modify all colour maps so that the minimum, nan and None values are set to black

  • figsize (tuple) – size of the figure, used if axs is None

  • titles (list) – title of each wedge

  • norms (list) – colour normalisation of each wedge: “log”, “linear” or a matplotlib.colors.Normalize If None, all are “log”

  • kwargs (dict) – All additional arguments to be passed onto the add_wedge and add_beam_axes functions

add_wedge(ax, *args, **kwargs)[source]

Add a wedge onto the plot, drawn with the stored axes extent.

add_beam_axes(ax, *args, **kwargs)[source]

Add axes, labels and ticks to the split beam plot, using the stored cosmology.
